title: Definition of the composition of the mitochondrial nucleoid in mice
projectDescription: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is compacted into dynamic structures called mitochondrial nucleoids (mt-nucleoids), with the mitochondrial transcription factor A (TFAM) as the core packaging protein. We generated Tfam-FLAGBAC mice to investigate the mt-nucleoid composition in vivo. Importantly, we showed that the TFAM-FLAG protein is functional and complements the absence of the wild-type TFAM. We identified proteins as core mt-nucleoid components by proteomics analysis of Tfam-FLAGBAC mice. Surprisingly, the mitoribosome subunit MRPS38 was part of the mt-nucleoid, and its downregulation led to the increase of mtDNA replication and transcription. Thus, MRPS38 might have a novel function repressing mtDNA expression. Also, we identified proteins that may stabilize TFAM-FLAG upon depletion of the mitochondrial RNA polymerase despite the absence of mtDNA and induction of the LONP1 protease. Finally, we evaluated the changes in mt-nucleoids caused by very high levels of TFAM-FLAG and discovered eight new interactors that could counteract the high TFAM levels to maintain active mtDNA transcription. Altogether, we demonstrate that the Tfam-FLAGBAC mice are a valuable tool for investigating the mt-nucleoid composition in vivo.
sampleProcessingProtocol: 500 ug of crude mitochondria were pelleted and resuspended in 150 uL of lysis buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 150 mM or 20 mM NaCl, 5 mM MgCl2, 1 % n-dodecyl-ÃŽÂ²-D-maltoside (DDM) and protease inhibitors (Complete EDTA-free, Roche)).  Lysis was conducted on ice before clearing at 16,000g for 5 min. The supernatant was diluted ten times with wash buffer (50 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.4, 100 or 20 mM NaCl, and 5 mM MgCl2) and incubated with 100 uL of anti-FLAG M2 beads (Sigma-Aldrich) for 2 h at 4Ã‚Â°C. The beads were previously equilibrated in wash buffer supplemented with 0.1% DDM. Afterward, the beads were washed three times with wash buffer supplemented with 0.1% DDM and three times with wash buffer without detergent. The beads were resuspended in 200 uL and were supplemented with 15 Ã‚ÂµL of 8M urea and 1 Ã‚Âµg trypsin (sequencing grade, Promega) in 105 Ã‚ÂµL of 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, and incubated at room temperature (RT) for 30 min with shaking at 400 rpm. The samples were centrifuged at 7000 rpm for 30 s before the supernatant was collected (ca. 120 Ã‚ÂµL) in new tubes. The beads were washed with 75 Ã‚ÂµL of 1M urea in 50 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, and 1 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) and with 100 mM Tris-HCl collecting the supernatant in the same tube (total ca. 195 Ã‚ÂµL). Digestion in the eluent was continued overnight at RT adding 5 Ã‚ÂµL of 0.1 Ã‚Âµg/Ã‚ÂµL trypsin with shaking at 400 rpm, while the agarose beads were supplemented with 45 Ã‚ÂµL of 1M urea and 1 mM DTT and 1 Ã‚Âµg trypsin in 35 Ã‚ÂµL of 100 mM Tris-HCl and further digested overnight at RT with shaking at 400 rpm. The peptide solutions were alkylated with 2 or 4 Ã‚ÂµL of 250 mM iodoacetamide in 50 mM of Tris-HCl incubating at RT for 30 min in the dark. The digestion was stopped with 14 Ã‚ÂµL of cc. formic acid (FA) in the combined peptide solution and samples were cleaned on a C-18 HyperSep plate (Thermo Scientific) and dried in a vacuum concentrator (Eppendorf).  Peptides were reconstituted in 10 Ã‚ÂµL of solvent A (0.1% FA in water) and 2 Ã‚ÂµL was injected on a 50 cm long EASY-Spray C18 column (Thermo Fisher Scientific) connected to an Ultimate 3000 nanoUPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) using a 90 min long gradient: 4-26% of solvent B (98% acetonitrile, 0.1% FA) in 90 min, 26-95% in 5 min, and 95% of solvent B for 5 min at a flow rate of 300 nL/min. Mass spectra were acquired on a Q Exactive HF hybrid quadrupole Orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) ranging from m/z 375 to 1500 at a resolution of R=120,000 (at m/z 200) targeting 5x106 ions for maximum injection time of 100 ms, followed by data-dependent higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) fragmentations of precursor ions with a charge state 2+ to 8+, using 30 s dynamic exclusion. The tandem mass spectra of the top 17 precursor ions were acquired with a resolution of R=30,000, targeting 2x105 ions for a maximum injection time of 54 ms, setting quadrupole isolation width to 1.4 Th and normalized collision energy to 28%.
dataProcessingProtocol: The raw data were processed using MaxQuant version 1.6.10.43. The search database was the UniProt mouse proteome UP000000589 as of 20191022 and default parameters were used. The protein groups reports were used for further analysis. Quantitative data were either log2-transformed (WT_13_weeks_FLAG_IP data) or cyclic loess normalized and log2 transformed (CAG_TFAM_and_Polrmt_KO_FLAG_IP data) using NormalyzerDE. Differential expression analysis was performed in NormalyzerDE without imputation and further pairwise between groups using LIMMA after imputation of a value corresponding to the lowest value observed in the batch to groups with all missing values if at least three values were found in the comparison group.
